funder: Paul Mellon Centre for Studies in British Art

records.justification: All claims made in the agent's text are directly supported by the provided page text, which details the funding round, deadlines, purposes, amounts, and application processes.

claims.text: Grant applications for the Autumn 2026 round of funding are open.
Grant applications will close on Monday 14 September at 11:59pm BST.
This funding round is the first since a new funding structure was announced earlier this year.
The funding is for research projects in the field of British art, visual culture, and architectural history.

There is a new grant of up to £40,000 for organizations undertaking ambitious and sustained research in British art, visual culture, and architectural history, including elements of three previous grant types.
The £40,000 grant is primarily to support staff costs for research projects with public-facing outcomes and/or legacy.
Outcomes for the £40,000 grant can include exhibitions, digital projects, catalogues, or similar dissemination forms.
Grants of up to £6,000 are available to support individuals disseminating research on British art through publications.
The £6,000 grant for individuals can support practical publishing costs like image copyright fees.
Grants of up to £6,000 are available to support organizations producing publications related to their exhibitions and displays.
The £6,000 grant for organizations can support publishing costs such as image and production costs.
Grants of up to £5,000 are available to support organizations digitizing collections to make them freely available online.
The £5,000 grant can support personnel costs and equipment for digitization projects.
Grants of up to £3,000 are available to support organizations disseminating research on British art through events.
The £3,000 grant can support costs such as venue hire, accommodation for speakers, and staffing for events.
Grants of up to £25,000 are available to help protect and preserve significant works of British art through conservation research.
The £25,000 grant can support staff costs and equipment for conservation research projects.
General application guidance, updated FAQs, and information on funding focus are available to assist applicants.
Information about previously successful projects and people is available.
Applicants with specific questions can contact the Grants team via email.
